base disorders in intensive care unit patients , their comorbidities and outcomes"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETITLE:\u0026nbsp;ACID BASE DISORDERS IN INTENSIVE CARE UNIT PATIENTS, THEIR CO-MORBIDITIES AND OUTCOMES\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EINTRODUCTION:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe hydrogen-ion concentration is tightly regulated because changes in hydrogen ions alter virtually all protein and membrane functions.(6)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe first step in assessment of an acid–base disorder is a careful clinical evaluation. Various signs and symptoms often provide clues regarding the underlying acid–base disorder;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ethese include the patient's vital signs (which may indicate shock or sepsis), neurologic state (consciousness vs. unconsciousness), signs of infection (e.g., fever), pulmonary status (respiratory rate and presence or absence of Kussmaul respiration, cyanosis, and clubbing of the fingers), and gastrointestinal symptoms (vomiting and diarrhea).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECertain underlying medical conditions such as pregnancy, diabetes, and heart, lung, liver, and kidney disease may also hint at the cause.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe clinician should determine whether the patient has taken any medications that affect acid–base balance (e.g., laxatives, diuretics, topiramate, or metformin) and should consider signs of intoxication that may be associated with acid–base disturbances (e.g., acetone fetor as a sign of diabetic ketoacidosis or isopropyl alcohol intoxication, and visual disturbance as a symptom of methanol intoxication). (4)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe three major methods of quantifying acid–base disorders are the physiological approach, the base-excess approach, and the physicochemical approach (also called the Stewart method). (5)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENeed for the study:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAcid–base homeostasis exerts a major influence on protein function, thereby critically affecting tissue and organ performance. (1)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChanges in blood pH in either direction are associated with higher mortality. (2)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ewhen severe, can be life-threatening. Yet it is the nature of the condition responsible for severe acidemia or alkalemia that largely determines the patient's status and prognosis. (1)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhereas a blood pH of 7.10 can be of little consequence when caused by a transient or easily reversible condition, such as an isolated seizure, it forecasts an ominous outcome if it is the result of methanol intoxication.(1)\u000B\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENormal blood pH is between 7.36 and 7.44, which corresponds to a hydrogen ion concentration of 44–36 nmol\/L. When pH is \u0026lt;7.36, an acidemia is present, whereas when it is \u0026gt;7.44 an alkalemia exists. It needs to be stressed, however, that because multiple acid-base disorders can exist simultaneously, the pH may be in the normal range. Hence, the clinician needs to follow a systematic approach to identify the underlying disorders.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETherefore, the ability to identify these acid-base disorders, understand the underlying pathophysiology, and provide appropriate therapy is paramount to the care of patients who are critically ill. (3)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAIM\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETo evaluate various acid base disturbances in intensive care unit patients, their co-morbidities and outcomes\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EObjectives:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. To study clinical profile in patients with acid base disturbances.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.To elicit various acid base disturbance in medical intensive care unit.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3.To elicit the causes for acid base disturbances.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4.To study the effect of pH on the prognosis of the diseases.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMATERIALS AND METHODS:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPlace of study\u003C\/b\u003E: Department of general medicine, Kamineni institute of medical sciences, narketpally\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EStudy period\u003C\/b\u003E: January 2024 to December 2025.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EStudy design\u003C\/b\u003E:\u0026nbsp;Qualitative, Prospective and Observational study that evaluates each thematic category of patient illness event data into diagnostically labeled morbidities as well as comorbidities and establishes a relation between their intervention outcomes over time\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003Esample size\u003C\/b\u003E: 50\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1) Patients of any gender above or equal to 18yrs of age at the time of presentation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) Patients having abnormal ABG analysis due to any eitiology are selected by simple random sampling from
